title: Year 12 source-demand editorial review

source.title: SCSA Computer Science ATAR Year 12 syllabus for teaching from 2027
source.method: Official course-page listing and official PDF web rendition inspected 2026-10-31; printed unit-content pages 8–19. PDF page is 1-based printed page + 4. No binary-hash verification claimed.
source.locatorConvention: item-map editorial bullet numbering, counting parent and nested markers. Only leaves assigned; web lines refer to official PDF rendition.

scope: Year 12 Units 3–4; Year 11 teaching-from-2026 foundation preserved. Source demand headings are concise paraphrases; rationale judges existing textbook depth.

judgementMeaning.supported: Substantive explanation/example and relevant learner practice are provided. Resource support does not establish mastery, teacher approval or formal assessment coverage.
judgementMeaning.partial: Specified depth, alignment or practice weakness remains.

limitations: Independent teacher/symbol review and actual learner performance remain pending.
Conditional debugger, simulator and ping/traceroute exercises are practice opportunities; execution/results are not claimed.
School-issued formal assessment coverage is outside this teaching-content review.
Legal and cryptographic references need teaching-time currency checks; this file does not supply operational/legal advice.
Editorial evidence supersedes weak automated candidate retrieval without changing item-map statuses.
Only this new review file is authored.

sections: Choose and trace loop forms

reviews.rationale: Fixed/pre/post tests contrast n=0 and n=3, including the at-least-once post-test. Selection and sequence are also constructed in the counter scaffold.

sections: Retrieve types, operators and Boolean precedence

reviews.rationale: Counts, approximate measurements, leading-zero identifiers and explicit text-to-Boolean conversion justify all four types. Boolean B012 has direct support despite its null candidate location.

sections: Parameters: mutation and rebinding
Scope and Python argument binding

reviews.rationale: Caller scalar/list outputs distinguish local rebinding, shared mutation and scope. Python argument assignment is accurately explained alongside course value/reference terminology; generic parsing examples were weaker candidates.

sections: Choose the structure for the question
Traverse rows and columns
Build and use a dictionary

reviews.rationale: Grid traversal, independent rows and dictionary lookup/update/removal are explained with contracts. E1 requires fresh pseudocode traversal and dictionary work, matching the source pseudocode skill more closely than a Python-only candidate module.

sections: Retrieve types, operators and Boolean precedence
State the contract before writing code

reviews.rationale: The blocked/trained/supervisor example compares grouped and ungrouped expressions and all eight combinations. Equality boundaries and arithmetic/relational/logical operators are applied in the counter.

sections: Turn the problem into measurable requirements
Develop one tested slice at a time
Submit evidence and evaluate against the requirements
Worked Gantt schedule and dependencies

reviews.rationale: Current actor-game FR/NFR criteria, scheduled dependencies, design, iterations and evaluation provide concrete stages. Keep these requirements distinct from legacy console-loan illustrations elsewhere.

sections: Compare development processes

reviews.rationale: A stable counter requirement then a threshold change makes linear-versus-iterative tradeoffs concrete and asks learners to apply the stages.

sections: Separate validation, processing and display
Preserve versions and prove recovery

evidence.section: unit3-reliability — Review developer responsibilities through scenarios

reviews.rationale: Parser conversion/domain checks distinguish valid zero from rejection; processing/display and single-purpose functions are separated. Explicit stubs, exceptions, returned structures, meaningful versions and tested recovery are explained. Reliability responsibility scenarios add ethical cases; a returned collection is one structure, not several unrelated returns.

sections: Scope and Python argument binding
Convention-focused transfer

reviews.rationale: Fresh algorithm representation, functions, arguments and explicit stubs are required. Objects/inheritance workbook A also implements class modularity. E1 supplies independent pseudocode rather than assuming that reading the search example is enough.

sections: Linear search: check in order
Binary search: discard half
Desk-check the bounds
Compare growth, not just a stopwatch

reviews.rationale: Sortedness, duplicates, missing targets and shrinking bounds are traced. Growth analysis separates probes from Boolean comparisons, best/worst cases and preparation cost. The absent-target n=8/16/32/1024 task is stronger than the candidate sorting-contract example for Big O purpose.

sections: Bubble sort: move the largest to the end
Insertion sort: grow a sorted prefix
Selection sort: place the smallest remaining item
Compare growth and the work being counted

reviews.rationale: All three mechanisms have pseudocode, Python, pass tables and consistent key-comparison counts. Early-exit bubble/insertion best cases differ from quadratic selection and worst cases; fresh copies preserve duplicates and mutation contracts. Insertion support belongs here, not in candidate search links.

sections: Start with a requirement and an expected result
Choose normal, boundary and rejected data
Plan a representative load and file-size trial

evidence.kind: current game acceptance and performance evidence
evidence.section: 2. Trace every shared requirement — FR1–FR10 and NFR1–NFR7

reviews.rationale: Expected/actual fixtures, unit/integration/acceptance distinctions, synthetic mixed transactions, file bytes and timings are substantial. Current game workbook FR1–FR10 and NFR1–NFR7 also give concrete acceptance/reliability/responsiveness criteria, so independent testing tasks are available. The remaining weakness is alignment: reliability still calls the console-loan R5/R9 and imports project_reference.py while the current adopted project is the actor game. Learners need an explicit distinction and adaptation path; loan workload measurements are not game performance evidence.
actions: Label the console-loan case as a separate worked example; add explicit navigation/adaptation from its testing concepts to the current game workbook FR/NFR criteria, including representative files/workload and actual response measures.

proposedOriginalTask.prompt: For the current actor game, predict pause/resume and restart trials. Record score, lives, gameplay time and actor states; pause three seconds, resume, then restart. Design a bounded many-actor workload and a large resource-file case. State machine/version, workload, response criterion and expected state before measurement.
proposedOriginalTask.answerSuggestions: Pause preserves gameplay state/time while event handling remains responsive; resume continues state and restart restores specified initial values. Count and frame-time checks must use stated workload/environment and expected actor/state assertions. Report synthetic/target differences and actual measured limits; no universal timing pass mark is implied.
proposedOriginalTask.status: optional bridge proposal addressing alignment; existing game acceptance tasks already available; not integrated or independently reviewed

sections: Isolate a fault before changing code

reviews.rationale: Syntax/logic/division-by-zero/index faults have concrete distinctions. The double-return defect gives minimal reproduction, expected/actual state and regression retest. E2 explicitly requires breakpoint watch/step evidence; actual learner use remains unobserved.

sections: Design the class before coding
Instantiate and initialise
Methods: queries and commands
Separate instances, shared aliases and class attributes

reviews.rationale: Equipment validation, independent instances, alias versus class-state trace and query/command methods demonstrate state and control structures. Workbook construction and changed-state tests go beyond naming concepts.

sections: Override behaviour while keeping the interface
Polymorphism: one call, different implementations
Abstraction and a consistent stock contract

evidence.section: A — Model and initialise; B — Dispatch and abstraction; C — Contracts and testing

reviews.rationale: Mixed receivers select their own preparation implementation; adding AudioRecorder leaves the report unchanged. super initialisation, inherited methods and common contracts distinguish actual polymorphism from merely defining subclasses. Objects chapter Encapsulation and abstraction explains underscore conventions and method-controlled invariants without calling them a security boundary.

sections: Review developer responsibilities through scenarios

reviews.rationale: Installer provenance, sole-record reliance, public social posts, cyber safety and unsupported web facts each connect stakeholders/consequences to a developer response.

sections: Review developer responsibilities through scenarios
Maintain versions, backups and honest limitations

reviews.rationale: Source/permission records and recognition, quality and user fault response, conduct, avoiding malware, ergonomics/inclusion and privacy receive distinct cases. The accessible feedback and disclosure cases are better evidence than generic test-harness candidates.

sections: Compare the seven-layer OSI and four-layer TCP/IP models
Distinguish layer 2 switching from layer 3 routing

evidence.section: A — Layers and nested units; B — Follow a routed message

reviews.rationale: Seven/four-layer role mapping and a per-hop path distinguish MAC switching and IP routing. DoD network/link is not confused with OSI network; the original routed-path diagram makes the conceptual mapping concrete.

sections: Compare TCP and UDP behaviour
Read transport fields and trace a TCP connection

reviews.rationale: Header fields, handshake/sequence/acknowledgements and UDP structure are compared. File/media choices include counterexamples rather than conflating reliability with encryption.

sections: An address needs a prefix
Distinguish RFC 1918 private, public and special addresses
Convert a prefix to a mask and a capacity
Compare IPv6 and read its notation

reviews.rationale: Prefix/mask and host-to-subnet arithmetic cover both IP versions and private/public distinctions. Special/documentation blocks are not labelled private; IPv6 does not inherit the ordinary IPv4 broadcast subtraction rule.

sections: Separate ports, IP addresses and link addresses

evidence.section: B — Follow a routed message; C — Transport choices and fields

reviews.rationale: Remote TCP/443 routing separates MAC, IP and port and contrasts DNS with local ARP. Addressing chapter Decide local versus routed and validate a gateway provides the gateway calculation. A translation-only gateway module is insufficient for DNS/ports.

sections: Follow encapsulation and decapsulation
Calculate sizes using explicit assumptions

evidence.section: A — Layers and nested units; D — Size and diagnose

reviews.rationale: Nested units and header/padding assumptions give conceptual and numerical examples from payload to bits; this directly replaces irrelevant generic gateway candidates.

sections: Build and check a variable-length address plan
Verify the arithmetic and diagnose mistakes

reviews.rationale: A fresh parent /24 requires smallest aligned nonoverlapping LANs, gateways and reserve, with actual isolated simulator/lab application. Workbook/calculator support planning. Application is conditional on an assigned environment; paper calculation alone does not demonstrate it.

sections: Choose components by their role

reviews.rationale: Media/modem/router/gateway/switch/AP/firewall each has a role, design choice and multifunction-device caveat. This chapter is stronger than sending all device bullets to a generic gateway depth module.

sections: Draw physical and logical topology
Separate broadcast domains and enforce policy
Calculate capacity and identify bottlenecks

reviews.rationale: Labelled intermediate/end nodes, topology, demand/capacity and enforced segmentation connect to staff/visitor requirements. Uplink changes and local versus internet paths support justified performance choices.

sections: Use ping and traceroute as evidence

reviews.rationale: Synthetic interpretation models cautious conclusions; E6 requires bounded actual ping/traceroute on an assigned authorised target, saved timestamps/load and independent service checks. Resource provision is supported while learner execution and access remain unobserved.

sections: Course diagram convention and live evidence

reviews.rationale: E5 supplies support-booklet page 12, Cisco symbols, perimeter placement and labelled subnets/endpoints/link media/rates. Redrawing and interpretation go beyond the concept diagram. Independent symbol fidelity remains pending.

sections: Turn APP 11 into design evidence
Assess a federal notifiable breach case
Identify whose privacy rules apply

reviews.rationale: Entity/date assumptions, protection/retention, serious harm/remediation and assessment versus notification are applied to case facts. Federal APP coverage is distinguished from WA public-sector law. This audit checks prescribed teaching content; linked primary law still needs teaching-time checks.

sections: Classify threats without treating labels as proof
Build an evidence-based incident hypothesis

evidence.section: twelve scenario cards and hypothesis record

reviews.rationale: Phishing, DoS/DDoS, back door, spoofing, injection, interception and XSS have mechanisms and discriminating clues. Scenario responses require observations, alternatives and next evidence rather than treating one log entry as proof.

sections: Classify threats without treating labels as proof

reviews.rationale: The table differentiates host-attaching virus, self-propagating worm, disguised trojan, spyware, adware and ransomware, plus physical and zero-day exposure. Direct examples support every listed mechanism; no malware execution is needed.

sections: Classify threats without treating labels as proof
Read a synthetic event sequence

reviews.rationale: Lost devices, credentials and employee misuse connect to specific assets/evidence. Accepted login and allowed export are distinguished from proof of a human actor or malicious intent.

sections: Compare the required control families
Write narrow traffic rules and inspect order
Separate identity, role and resource scope
Write acceptance tests and residual risks

evidence.section: ordered rules, role matrix and response cases

reviews.rationale: Every prescribed control has purpose/evidence/limits, including training, conduct and physical security. First-match shadowing, trusted record-scope checks and positive/negative scenarios directly exercise mitigation; candidate event-cleaning examples were not adequate substitutes.

sections: Apply the CIA triad to specific consequences
Distinguish the AAA questions

reviews.rationale: Booking consequences distinguish all three security goals and identity/permission/audit functions. Allowed export versus denied delete supplies an authorisation example; accounting is audit evidence, not financial calculation. Applied cases are stronger than generic cleaning links.

sections: Keep key roles separate
Explain certificates and trust
Trace a simplified TLS 1.3 connection

reviews.rationale: Symmetric confidentiality, public/private encryption/signature roles and certificate trust are distinguished. TLS uses authenticated ephemeral agreement then symmetric records; it avoids the false TLS 1.3 RSA session-key-transport account. Independent cards/ordering ask reasoning about remaining export risks.

sections: From historical ciphers to modern algorithms

reviews.rationale: Historical substitution/repeated-key weaknesses contrast with modern algorithm roles and implementation/key-management limits. Caesar brute-force demonstrates weakness rather than recommending deployment. Maintained primary references support future currency checks.

sections: Explain ethical hacking and team roles

reviews.rationale: Authority, targets/time/techniques/exclusions, handling and reporting are explicit. Red emulation, blue defence and remediation/retest have distinct roles. Paper scope supports the knowledge demand without claiming live penetration testing.

sections: Read the six-table crow’s-foot model
Write relational notation and key rules
Make a data dictionary that matches implementation

reviews.rationale: The six-table model covers entities/attributes/records, cardinalities, conceptual types and joint keys. Attendance composite FK explains why independent references are insufficient. Date/Boolean concepts are separated from SQLite storage affinity. D requests a fresh six-entity design.

sections: Diagnose a flat record and its dependencies

evidence.section: A — flat relation anomalies and dependencies

reviews.rationale: Repeated instructor facts, unbooked sessions and last-booking deletion show update/insert/delete anomalies. Learners explain consequences before decomposing; the answer sheet gives the dependency reasoning.

sections: Use transactions to protect a booking

evidence.section: Transaction walkthrough: one request, one boundary

reviews.rationale: ODBC is correctly named as driver-based and distinguished from sqlite3 DB-API, but only a short comparison describes its architecture. The reference demonstrates direct SQLite, not a worked driver/application/result path. The source is a knowledge demand, so an installed ODBC lab is not required; an explanatory example and independent comparison would improve depth.
actions: Add a worked ODBC driver/data-source/application/results diagram and a separate learner explanation task; retain accurate distinction from direct SQLite.

proposedOriginalTask.prompt: An attendance application accesses a supported school DBMS using ODBC. Draw the request/result path through application, ODBC interface, selected driver and DBMS. Explain what might change for another DBMS and why a direct Python sqlite3 call does not demonstrate ODBC.
proposedOriginalTask.answerSuggestions: The application issues requests through ODBC; the suitable driver communicates with its DBMS and returns results/errors. Driver/configuration and possibly DBMS-specific SQL change; ODBC does not unify every SQL dialect. sqlite3 is a direct DB-API route to SQLite without an ODBC driver.
proposedOriginalTask.status: proposal, not integrated or independently reviewed

sections: Use transactions to protect a booking

evidence.section: Transaction walkthrough: one request, one boundary; Read the reference boundary before reusing a function

reviews.rationale: All four ACID properties connect to last-place competition and all-or-none changes. The workbook notes book commits separately from set_attendance: a later failure cannot undo an earlier commit. Explicit rollback/before-after checks support atomicity while in-memory success is not crash durability.

sections: Read the six-table crow’s-foot model
Write relational notation and key rules
Make a data dictionary that matches implementation
Transfer to a fresh design

reviews.rationale: The fresh six-entity creation task fits the required range and includes notation/dictionary/bridge resolution. The separate ten-table interpretation workbook reaches the maximum diagram size with optionality and composite references. This corrects candidate anomaly modules that cannot by themselves establish diagram interpretation.

sections: Distinguish three kinds of integrity
Compare conceptual rules with a runnable schema

evidence.section: C — predicted constraint outcomes and unenforced rules

reviews.rationale: Duplicate keys, orphans and invalid Present/capacity values distinguish entity, referential and domain integrity. The checker contrasts intended rules with actual enforcement; well-formed dates and valid values do not prove factual accuracy.

sections: Distinguish three kinds of integrity

reviews.rationale: The dedicated quality worksheet supplies dates/provenance/units/source evidence for every factor. Microphones 80 versus 8 separate validation from accuracy; supplier stock relevance, archive currency, unknown uploader authenticity and verified chair extremes demand different decisions. This closes weak/null candidate links, especially relevance.

sections: Diagnose a flat record and its dependencies
Write relational notation and key rules

evidence.section: A — decompose flat relation; D — fresh model

reviews.rationale: Atomic domains/repeating lists, partial candidate-key dependencies and transitive dependencies precede decomposition. A/D require relational notation and new-model transfer. Adding a surrogate ID is explicitly rejected as a cure for remaining dependencies.

sections: Define the report’s grain
Join up to four tables and keep keys visible
Aggregate at the correct grain
Calculate and concatenate with aliases

reviews.rationale: Four-table key paths, all five aggregates, grouping/ordering and calculated/concatenated aliases are taught and exercised. NULL/zero, real division and repeated-capacity traps develop reasoning beyond syntax. Fresh transfers require predictions before execution.

sections: Make controlled changes and verify effects

reviews.rationale: R1 requires actual six-table implementation/inspection; R6 and the disposable change lab cover CREATE/ALTER/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/cascade/DROP with references/constraints. Source MODIFY means modifying the schema through the chosen DBMS, not inventing a SQLite MODIFY keyword. A reference download alone is not learner construction.

sections: Clean an import without inventing data

evidence.section: Develop; R5 atomic synthetic member batch

reviews.rationale: Raw fields are mapped and validated; missing names are not invented and invalid/duplicate batches must leave rows unchanged. Raw/clean CSVs and scaffold make import concrete. Event-log cleaning is extension rather than a substitute for database-import work.

sections: Collect and analyse data responsibly
Acknowledge sources and plan an open resource

reviews.rationale: Purpose/minimisation, privacy, appropriate use, source reliability/acknowledgement and mining bias connect to booking decisions. Aggregate support versus punitive profiling and possible re-identification develop the ethical consequences rather than equating removed names with anonymity.

sections: Turn APP 11 into design evidence
Collect and analyse data responsibly

reviews.rationale: Privacy, recoverable backups, restricted exports and ownership/control connect to purpose/stakeholders. Separate application/network controls include positive/negative tests. Encryption alone is not offered as a complete protection argument.

sections: Identify whose privacy rules apply
Apply the five prescribed APPs

reviews.rationale: Each prescribed APP is connected to a distinct collection/overseas disclosure/quality/protection/access decision. Case responses require entity/jurisdiction/date and missing facts rather than automatically applying federal rules to a WA public school.

summary.coverageValidation: Every Year12 leaf ID assigned exactly once; all cited local evidence paths exist and named explanation sections match parsed chapter sections.
